Encore 0.2.1 fixes playback in the Linux AppImage and the system title bar setting.

## Download

| System | File |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) | `Encore_0.2.1_universal.dmg` |
| Windows 10 and 11 | `Encore_0.2.1_x64-setup.exe` (or the `.msi`) |
| Debian, Ubuntu | `Encore_0.2.1_amd64.deb` |
| Other Linux | `Encore_0.2.1_amd64.AppImage` |

Playback needs **Python 3.10+** and **Node.js, Deno or Bun** installed. See
[Install](https://github.com/Nayhap/encore#install) for one-line commands.

## First launch

These builds are not code-signed yet.

- **macOS:** open the app once, then go to **System Settings → Privacy &
  Security** and choose **Open Anyway**. macOS asks once for access to your
  saved session in the Keychain.
- **Windows:** SmartScreen warns on first run. Choose **More info**, then
  **Run anyway**. If Smart App Control is on, Windows blocks the app.

## Fixes

- **Linux AppImage:** songs wouldn't play, with "creating the resolver venv
  failed: <no Python frame>". The AppImage's launcher points Python at files
  inside the AppImage, and Encore passed that on when it set up yt-dlp with
  your system Python. Encore now gives Python a clean environment.
- **Use the system title bar** (Windows and Linux) now takes effect. On Linux,
  Encore restarts to apply it, because the desktop ignores the change on a
  window that's already open.
- Setup errors now show the line that says what went wrong, not the last
  line of Python's crash report.
